intake: atheist — everything is physical, the mind is the brain working, and when the brain stops so does the person.

walk.note: That is simply what happened to me as a child; nobody asks you.
Books are written by people, so if you want a God you have to look outside the books; fair enough.
You look and all you find is stories and a 'first cause' that does nothing.
If prayer worked the hospitals would know it by now.
The mind does reduce to matter; take a blow to the head and see. Nothing about this needs a soul.
Yes, this is what I would have said at move 5; a ghost with no fingerprints does nothing.
Fine, call it physics instead of matter; this is where I live.
Physics not telling you 'what has the structure' does not make the world a dream; that is a jump, not a step.
Granting the dream, yes, somebody has to be asleep, and it is a brain.
Other people have brains, so other people have insides; obvious.
I would treat them decently too, though I would just call it being decent, not Mercy with a capital letter.
Being kind to people does not hand you 'learned ignorance', and I cannot tell what entropy or someone called Claude are doing in this move.
The move itself admits a secular hope or equanimity is open; I take equanimity, and a death is a death whatever you hope.
The last sentence says it outright: being a maker does not make a maker resolved, so the move cancels itself.
A bargain with whom, about what? There is no move written here.
A mind that attends to everything is not doing anything I would call thinking; I would have gotten here anyway by lack of evidence.
Pain is bad for the one in pain, maker or no maker; this is the plainest line on the map.
Wanting to be remembered does not split you into two things; the move even says the need is not evidence.
Nothing is claimed here except that there is no data, and 'ceiling and floor' tells me nothing.

first_exit.why: The move says that without God the mind still does not seem to reduce to matter. It does. Every memory, mood and decision changes when the brain changes, and the map itself says so one move later, so I never had a reason to stop at Dualism.

comment: You had the answer at move 7 and everything after move 8 reads like wanting it to be otherwise. Moves 12, 15 and 19 are not moves, they are gaps with names on them; say plainly what is being claimed or cut them. Treating people well does not need a spiral behind it.
